supersession.no_opening_under_either: No sealed opening occurred under v1.0 or v2.0. Neither was ever executed against AWS: no credential assumed, no host started under them, no GetObject issued.

v1.0.why: no entry point, no production reader, fixture-assembled world, both frozen earnings controls absent

v2.0.why: closure defined by a hand-maintained list: 35 bound and 35 imported but not the same 35, leaving spq1/__init__.py unbound while it supplied PHASE0_CENSUS_SHA256, PHASE0_OWNER_RULINGS_SHA256, PHASE0_SCHEMA_SHA256 and PRODUCER_CODE_VERSION into GOVERNING_IDENTITIES and thus every record

v3.0.why: its s3_reader built an ambient-credential S3 client with no STS path, so the first read would have been attempted as the qualified host role - which holds an explicit Deny on the sealed bucket and must keep it. The package reached S7 faithfully and could not cross it.

v3.1.opening_under_it: attempt #1 consumed the single opening under this execution identity and produced no usable result. The opening is SPENT and the attempt technically VOID.
v3.1.retained_from_it: the v3.1 PRIVILEGE-TRANSITION design is ACCEPTED and UNCHANGED: lazy STS, reader ARN as a module constant, temporary-credential-only S3 construction, no ambient fallback, host->reader Deny retained until a distinct owner event.
v3.1.why: its runner.py captured no primary_disposition/primary_error and its publish.py created no output root before asserting vacancy, so a publication exception replaced the computation's terminal verdict. That is the defect that rendered validation attempt #1 technically void. The package remains valid evidence for the privilege-transition design it established.
